findings.reason: the "blank field resolves the current directory" defect the section exists to remove is reachable through at least six paths outside promotion.py; hoisting `_record_tree` into one shared resolver that every reader calls — and widening §56's grep past promotion.py, as §45 did by enumerating callers — closes them all, whereas auditing promotion alone leaves the rest forking the rule.
findings.text: §56's done-when resolves sites through `_record_tree` and greps only `reckon/crew/promotion.py`, but `_record_tree`/`_record_worktree` are module-private to promotion.py, and the same "empty worktree field is absent, never `Path('.')`" rule is forked elsewhere: reckon/crew/recovery.py:5361 and :5411 build `Path(str(record.get("worktree...") or "."))`, reckon/crew/resumption.py:856 the same, and reckon/crew/dispatch.py:11908 and :12337 write `str(record.get("worktree") or ".")`

findings.reason: reports.py already owns manifest shape validation (`"baseline_suite"/"after_suite": frozenset({"text","mapping"})` at reports.py:139 and `suite_observation_missing_fields`), so the flat/keyed decision belongs in that one owner at check-manifest time; teaching two more readers a second shape is the parallel-reader defect §38 closed, and it is decided by the one party that cannot ask the worker to change the manifest.
findings.text: §48 offers as one of two options "the promotion guard and `_gate_log_path` accept a record keyed by arm", which would spread acceptance of a second suite-record shape across reckon/crew/promotion.py:5818

findings.reason: §51 names handing the worker its scratch as `TMPDIR` as the primary remedy and §57 is a lead ruling acknowledged as coming from the lead; extending `remove_worker_scratch` to reach the arms is the honest change but the reviewer records it as a note rather than a required plan change, because the ruling already sanctions the owner-side fix.
findings.text: §57 (a lead ruling) requires a passing run to clear every scratch arm it made, layered beside §51's `remove_worker_scratch` release rather than extending it, even though §51 already established the owner names the run's scratch by id

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §50 collapses the 27 literal `{"ok": True, **result}` sites in reckon/cli.py behind one outcome-derived helper, and §44/§45/§46 follow the same shape as §38 by putting many readers behind one resolver rather than spreading shallow accessors.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §56 audits the blank-worktree idiom only in reckon/crew/promotion.py, while the rule it enforces lives in the promotion-private `_record_tree`/`_record_worktree` and is re-implemented with the current-directory fallback in recovery.py, resumption.py and dispatch.py.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every pending section names the existing mechanism it extends (`_record_tree` at reckon/crew/promotion.py:7115 for §56, `worker_scratch_root`/`remove_worker_scratch` at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:8558 and :8556 for §51): no new subsystem is proposed.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §57 layers a worker-side scratch-clearing obligation on top of §51's release-side clearing, both over the same `worker_scratch_root()` owner, without saying why that owner cannot be extended to reach the arms.
